# Enzyme release notes - v0.13.2

## Short version

Fixes for four reported issues. Indexes built before the occurrence-weight
column open again after upgrading. A folder, tag, and link with the same name
no longer share a question budget or a leave-out. A local server can now get
hosted-size prompts, and a reply cut off at its output cap says so instead of
failing as unparseable JSON. `enzyme spec migrate` is retired; the setup skill
reads a legacy `config.toml` as evidence when it writes settings.

## What shipped

### Upgrading older indexes

- Indexes last opened by 0.9.1 or earlier, before the occurrence-weight
  column existed, failed every read-write command on 0.13.1 with
  `no such column: weight`, and read-only commands pointed at `enzyme refresh`,
  which failed the same way. The covering index from 0.13.1 is now created
  after the column migration, so these indexes upgrade in place and keep their
  catalysts. (#16, `0b3c603`)

### Selection

- Question budgets are keyed by entity name and type. A large folder no longer
  drops to the 3-question floor because a small tag or link with the same name
  was also selected. (#17, `e6cd7d1`)
- `leave out tags|links` removes only entities of that type. Leaving out the
  `[[writing]]` link no longer removes the `writing` folder, and folder
  expansion can no longer add a left-out link back. (#17, `e6cd7d1`)

### Bring-your-own model

- `ENZYME_LOCAL_MODEL=0` sends hosted-size prompts, job splitting, and the
  8,192-token output cap to a model served on localhost (LM Studio, Ollama, a
  llama.cpp server, or a local proxy in front of a remote provider). Localhost
  addresses otherwise keep the compact local-model path. (#19, `8e17451`)
- A reply that stops at the output cap before writing any answer, as reasoning
  models can, now fails with a message naming the cap. It is not retried with
  the same cap, and on the compact local path the message points to
  `ENZYME_LOCAL_MODEL=0`. (#15, `35c1259`)

### Settings

- `enzyme spec migrate` is removed. It refused any vault whose `config.toml`
  key went through a symlink, and nothing else used it. `config.toml` keeps
  working as before, and settings written for a vault take priority over its
  TOML section. The setup skill now reads a legacy `config.toml`, including its
  entity list, as evidence when it drafts settings. (#18, `5c20c29`)

## Behavior changes to check

- A folder exclusion or leave-out no longer removes tags or links that share
  its name; `exclude ["templates"]` keeps a `#templates` tag. Check
  `enzyme spec plan` if you relied on the old behavior.
- Scripts that call `enzyme spec migrate` will now fail with an unknown
  subcommand.
